page.title: Settings
page.purpose: Configure the operator's own console and the ceilings sessions run under. It does not configure governance: what a binding may do is declared in each scenario's CLI manifest and is never editable from here.

priorities.statement: Governance is shown as inherited, never as editable.
priorities.notes: effect, run_eligible, requires_confirmation, and permissions come from cli-manifest. A settings page that appeared to change them would create a second policy authority, which is the one thing the binding boundary must not have.

priorities.statement: Session ceilings state their units and their consequence.
priorities.notes: Lowering an idle ceiling reclaims kernels sooner and destroys handle state. The control should say that, not just accept a number.

priorities.statement: Operator grants are a deliberate act with a visible scope.
priorities.notes: Holding a destructive grant is the difference between reading the console and being able to break something from it.

priorities.statement: Every preference the console actually needs appears here.
priorities.notes: Theme, locale, font scale, editor preferences, accessibility options, and default corpus filters — not only whatever the template shipped.

states.description: Console preferences, session ceilings, and inherited governance are shown.
A change was persisted and the new value is reflected.
A submitted value is out of range and the accepted range is stated.
The operator lacks the grant required to change a setting; the control reads as unavailable with a reason rather than failing on submit.
Settings could not be read or written and the reason is visible.

elements.name: Editor
elements.description: Word wrap, whitespace rendering, and whether inline materialization decorations are shown by default.

elements.name: Accessibility
elements.description: Reduced motion, and whether the marker list is expanded by default alongside the editor.

elements.name: Session ceilings
elements.description: Idle, wall-clock, and memory limits, each with its unit and its consequence stated.

elements.name: Operator grants
elements.description: Which effects this operator may exercise from the console.

elements.name: Corpus defaults
elements.description: Default provenance filter and grouping for the program list.

elements.name: Governance is inherited
elements.description: States that binding governance is declared in each scenario's CLI manifest and is not editable here.

claims.statement: The page exposes a named settings region containing appearance, editor, accessibility, ceiling, grant, and corpus groups.
Binding governance is presented as inherited from cli-manifest and offers no editing affordance.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-005. This scenario enforces a governance contract it does not own. An editable copy here would be a second, divergent authority.

claims.statement: Each session ceiling states its unit and what happens when it is reached.
claims.rationale: OT-P1-005. Reclamation destroys kernel state, so a bare number with no stated consequence invites an operator to discard an agent's work by accident.

claims.statement: A setting the operator may not change reads as unavailable with a reason rather than failing after submission.
claims.rationale: A control that accepts input and then rejects it teaches operators that the console is unreliable.

claims.statement: An out-of-range ceiling reports the accepted range rather than a generic invalid message.
claims.rationale: Matches the voice contract the program page holds for pre-flight validation: name the field and the acceptable values.

claims.statement: Loading, saving, success, validation-error, permission-denied, and error states each render dedicated content.
Every control in every settings group is reachable and operable by keyboard alone.
